articles.title: Thought The Stars Of The Altruists Looked Familiar? Where You've Seen The Cast Before
articles.description: Earlier this week, Netflix unveiled a new drama to keep the platform’s legions of true crime fans gripped. The Altruists follows the real-life story of the so-called Bitcoin Bonnie and Clyde, Caroline Ellison and Sam Bankman-Fried. In 2022, the couple were at the helm of a cryptocurrency exchange firm, FTX, when it collapsed, leading to their arrests. This new show starring Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner documents the rise and fall of both their business and their romance. Alongside Anthony and Julia, The Altruists features a star-studded cast that includes a host of well-known actors and comedians, as well as familiar faces you might recognise from other popular Netflix shows. If you’ve been wondering why certain members of the cast looked familiar to you, here’s a quick guide to where you might have seen the cast of The Altruists before... Julia Garner Julia Garner as Anna Delvery in episode Inventing Anna The Altruists isn’t Julia Garner’s first time playing a famous convicted scammer. Before starring as Caroline Ellison, she took on the role of Anna Delvey in Netflix’s Inventing Anna, which explored the fake Russian heiress’ story. Besides Inventing Anna, Julia is perhaps best known for her Emmy-winning performance as the villainous Ruth in another Netflix crime drama, Ozark. Julia made her TV debut in 2015 in The Americans, playing the neglected teenager Kimberley, before appearing in shows like Waco, Maniac and Dirty John. Her film work has included Sin City: A Dame To Kill For and The Assistant, while last year she played both the Silver Surfer in The Fantastic Four: First Steps and Justine, a troubled teacher, in the surprise horror hit Weapons. Anthony Boyle Anthony Boyle in House Of Guinness Irish actor Anthony Boyle made a splash in 2024 when he played republican Brandan Hughes in Say Nothing, a Disney+ miniseries about the Northern Ireland Troubles. That same year, he starred alongside Austin Butler in the historical drama Masters Of The Air and Sean Bean in the C. J. Sansom adaptation Shardlake, as well as playing John Wilkes Booth to Hamish Linklater’s Abraham Lincoln in Manhunt. Netflix audiences will likely recognise Anthony for his leading role as Arthur Guinness in the Steven Knight drama House Of Guinness. He is also set to star alongside Joe Cole and Daryl McCormack in I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, a film about five working-class friends growing up in Birmingham, which hits cinemas next month. Alex Lawther Alex Lawther in The End Of The F***ing World Alex Lawther’s breakthrough came in 2015 when he was cast as Kenny in the Black Mirror episode Shut Up And Dance, about a boy who is blackmailed into committing crime by hackers. These days, he’s probably best recognised for playing James in The End Of The F***ing World or Karis Nemik in the Star Wars spin-off Andor. Last year, Alex appeared as Joe, the tactical officer and medic, in Alien: Earth, and as reserved writer Leonard in the Irish comedy Leonard And Hungry Paul. On film, Alex played a small role in Wes Anderson’s The French Dispatch, appeared as Charles VI in the historical drama The Last Duel and starred in the Paris-set drama A Second Life. Matt Rife Matt Rife performing stand-up at Madison Square Garden in 2023 Matt Rife is better known for his comedy specials and TikTok videos than his acting roles. He started his career as a cast member on the improv game show series Wild ’N Out, before landing small roles on the sitcoms Brooklyn Nine-Nine, Fresh Off The Boat and the recent reboot of Scrubs. Last year, Matt had a role in the horror film I Live Here Now with Lucy Fry and Madeline Brewer, and is set to star in the upcoming comedy movie Rolling Loud with Owen Wilson. Matt regularly hits the headlines for his controversial comedy, most notably in 2023 when he made a distasteful joke about domestic abuse victims or when he poked fun at a six-year-old online. Madison Hu Madison Hu as Fei in Avatar: The Last Airbender Madison Hu launched her career on the Disney Channel with recurring roles in the TV series Best Friends Whenever and the comedy Bizaardvark. She later gave supporting performances in the Netflix shows The Brother Sun, A Man On The Inside and Avatar: The Last Airbender, and starred alongside Steve Carell in the HBO comedy-drama Rooster earlier this year. In contrast to her comedic TV work, Madison’s film work consists of several horror films, like The Bad Words, Boogeyman and Night Shift. Karan Soni Karan Soni in Deadpool If you recognise Karan Soni, it’s more than likely for his role as the taxi driver Dopinder in the Deadpool franchise. Karan made his acting debut in 2012’s Safety Not Guaranteed, before making minor appearances in the 2016 reboot of Ghostbusters, the festive comedy Office Christmas Party and the Pokémon film Detective Pikachu. Since then, he has appeared alongside Jonathan Groff in the romance A Nice Indian Boy and voiced Spider-Man India in Spider-Man: Across The Spider-Verse. On TV, he has guest starred in numerous comedies including The Neighbors, The Goldbergs and Silicon Valley. Karan’s most notable small-screen role came in 2019 when he landed the lead in the anthology comedy Miracle Workers, playing an angel, cranky gunslinger and royal advisor alongside an ensemble cast which included Steve Buscemi and Daniel Radcliffe Earlier in 2026, he played minor roles as a lab doctor on the popular Apple TV+ drama Pluribus and a care facility warden in the Netflix sci-fi series The Boroughs. Paul Reiser Paul Reiser in Beverly Hills Cop Paul Reiser is best known for playing Det. Jeffrey Friedman in the Beverly Hills Cop franchise, as well as starring in, and creating, the popular 90s sitcom Mad About You. In more recent years, Paul has starred as Dr. Sam Owens in seasons two and three of Stranger Things, and was Emmy-nominated for his role as Mindy’s older boyfriend in The Kominsky Method. He also had a guest role as The Legend in The Boys and voiced Elliott in adult animation Long Story Short. On the big screen, he notably portrayed Jim, the father of the aspiring jazz drummer played by Miles Teller in Whiplash. His other recent credits include the funny action adventure The Spy Who Dumped Me, the psychological drama Horse Girl and the buddy comedy The Problem With People, which he also co-wrote. Jennifer Grey Jennifer Grey as Baby in the iconic Dirty Dancing Jennifer Grey is a true screen icon. Although she has had a long and illustrious career, you probably know her best for playing Baby in Dirty Dancing. Her other stand-out roles include playing the long-suffering older sister of Matthew Broderick’s title character in Ferris Bueller’s Day Off, high school student Toni in Red Dawn and the recently-divorced tour group member Marcia in A Real Pain. As for her work on TV, Jennifer played David’s mother Judy in the comedy drama Red Oaks, appeared as Betty’s birth mother Carol in season 15 of Grey Anatomy and had a guest role as Jackie’s friend Janelle in the sitcom The Conners. Robin Weigert Robin Weigert in Big Little Lies Robin Weigert is most recognisable for her Emmy-nominated turn as Calamity Jane in Deadwood. Her other notable roles include playing lawyer Ally Lowen in the biker drama Sons Of Anarchy, Jeri’s wife Wendy in Marvel’s Jessica Jones and Celeste’s therapist, Dr. Reisman, in Big Little Lies. Her more recent TV roles include Teddi in season one of Tracker, and the matriarch Nechuma Kurc in the historical drama We Were The Lucky Ones. Last year, she also reunited with her Sons Of Anarchy co-star Charlie Hunnam for Monster: The Ed Gein Story. Besides her TV roles, in 2013, Robin was nominated for a Gotham Award for her role in the indie movie Concussion, in which she played a woman who rethinks her life after a head injury. Robin’s other film credits include Bombshell, about the expose of sexual harassment at Fox News, the supernatural horror Smile and the dark comedy Tokyo Cowboy. Hudson Williams Hudson Williams in Heated Rivalry Unless you have been living under a rock, you’ll likely know Hudson Williams for playing Shane Hollander in the international phenomenon, Heated Rivalry. The Canadian actor also recently starred in the supernatural horror series Yaga alongside Carrie Anne Moss. He already has his next role lined up, starring in Tyrant alongside Charlize Theron, Demi Moore and his The Altruist co-star Julia Garner. Terry Chen Terry Chen in Almost Famous Terry Chen’s break-out role came when he starred as real-life Rolling Stone editor Ben Fong-Torres in 2000’s Almost Famous. His other movie work includes I, Robot, Snakes On A Plane and The Cabin In The Woods. Meanwhile, Terry’s television roles over the last three decades have included the cult classic Battlestar Galactica, sci-fi time travel drama Continuum and Netflix political drama House Of Cards. More recently, Terry played botanist Praxidike Meng in the space epic The Expanse, crown prosecutor Stan Lowe in true crime drama Under The Lake and master firebender Jeong Jeong in the live-action adaptation Avatar: The Last Airbender. William Mapother William Mapother in Lost William Mapother is widely recognised for playing Ethan Rom in Lost, a surgeon who forms part of the mysterious “Others”. His other TV credits include appearances in Prison Break as FBI Agent Chris Franco, The Mentalist as suspected paedophile Richard Haibach and Justified as season three’s bad guy Delroy Baker. On the big screen, William started his career appearing alongside his cousin Tom Cruise in the likes of Magnolia, Mission: Impossible 2 and Minority Report. His best-known film role is 2001’s In The Bedroom, in which he played Richard Stout, the movie’s main antagonist. Maddie Hasson Maddie Hasson in The Recruit Maddie Hasson is best known for playing headstrong teenager Willa Friday, the lead role in procedural drama The Finder. You might have also seen her in the teen drama Twisted, the sci-fi series Impulse or the Netflix spy thriller The Recruit. One of Maddie’s earliest film roles came when she portrayed the real-life country singer Billie Jean in the Hank Williams biopic I Saw the Light. Horror fans may also recognise Maddie for playing Madison’s sister, Sydney, in Malignant, while her other recent movie credits include the post-apocalyptic drama Elevation and the erotic thriller Bone Lake. Jack Greenlees Jack Greenlees in The Trial Of Christine Keeler Jack Greenlees first found fame playing Craig Cooper in the BBC series Shetland and has been a regular face on British screens since. His most notable early career appearances included playing the Familiar in gothic drama Penny Dreadful, Justice Knox in Harlots and Paul Mann in The Trial Of Christine Keeler. In 2024, Jack co-starred with Sophie Turner in ITV drama Joan, playing the police detective sympathetic to the titular character. Jack also appears in Strike as Sam Barclay, a soldier and rifleman the titular character hires for his agency. Last year, the Scottish star also acted in an episode of the Netflix crime drama Dept Q as an investigative reporter. The Altruists is now streaming in full on Netflix.
